newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: ST LUKES SEES CONTINUED EARNINGS GROWTH.
newsitem.headline: ST LUKES SEES CONTINUED EARNINGS GROWTH.

text.p: Shopping mall owner St Lukes Group expects to see continued strong earnings growth after posting its fourth consecutive record profit for the June year, chief executive Andrew Bennett said on Thursday.
Bennett said the NZ$31.15 million profit, which was up 8.6 percent on the previous year's, had come by virtue of strong assets.
"We are still of the view that there are many value-added opportunities left in this portfolio," Bennett told a briefing of analysts and journalists.
"We have an active management philosophy and a focused management team," he said. "We've got the right people on board, in terms of centre management and development management, in Westfield.
"This all leads to excellent prospects, so we expect to see continued growth in earnings and dividend payout," he said.
Glenfield was still a top priority and would be the next development to be carried out, he said.
Australia's Westfield, which took over commercial management of the St Lukes property porfolio earlier this year, was looking at Glenfield to make sure development potential would be optimised.
St Lukes expected to start the project some time next year but at this stage the feasibility had not been finalised.
Bennett said St Lukes' objective was to own regional shopping centres. "We see ourselves as a growth play...so it's unlikely that you would see us enter into pure income yielding types of assets."
St Lukes, which enjoyed occupancy rates of over 99 percent during the year, expected continued rental growth.
Proceeds from a NZ$90 million rights issue would be used for a variety of opportunities, both within and outside the existing portfolio.
Since listing, borrowings had increased to NZ$250 million from $112 million and part of the capital raised from the issue would be used to retire debt.
St Lukes is paying a 7.4 cent per share dividend which will, for the first time, carry a tax imputation credit.
Bennett said the Downtown Shopping Centre had been withdrawn from sale.
Sales at West City were expected to double to NZ$120 million as a result of redevelopment there, which is due for completion in April.
Riccarton Mall in Christchurch, which was bought in March for NZ$113 million, had potential for a revamp of its retail mix.
